doc: Plain-English explanations shown by the site (hand-written content, checked against STANDARDS.md section 4 and config/measure.json v1.3). tools/export_site_facts.py validates the feature ids and in_distance flags against config/measure.json and writes site/data/explain.json.

similarity.what: Two places are twins when their ground behaves alike: as steep, as rough, and shaped the same way (bowl, slope or plateau). It is a match of terrain behaviour, not of individual hills: laid on top of each other, the mountains do not line up.
similarity.distance: D combines three measures (steepness, bowl vs plateau, bumpiness), each scaled by how much it varies across the 2,000 Earth places. D = 0 means identical measures; smaller is closer.
similarity.ties: Measuring the same place twice with two different elevation models does not give D = 0: that spread is the measurement noise. Places whose D differs by less than that noise are tied: none of them is 'the' twin.

slope_p95_deg.label: Steepness
slope_p95_deg.what: The slope that 95% of the ground stays under, measured every 100 m.
slope_p95_deg.see_it: Turn on the slope layer: marked ground is steeper than the mission's landing (or driving) limit.
slope_p95_deg.why: Slopes are the first thing a landing or a traverse is checked against.

hi.label: Bowl vs plateau
hi.what: Where the average ground sits between the low and the high parts of the place (0 to 1). Low: mostly low ground with a few high spots, like a basin floor. High: mostly high ground cut by a few lows, like a plateau with channels.
hi.see_it: Draw a cross-section: a bowl stays low with raised edges, a plateau stays high with dips.
hi.why: It says whether a crew would mostly work on a floor, on slopes or on top.

hurst.label: Bumpiness across scales
hurst.what: How height differences grow from 100 m to 800 m steps. Near 1: smooth, rolling ground that changes gradually. Lower: ground that is already rough over short distances.
hurst.see_it: Look at the contour lines: long, gentle bends versus tight, broken ones.
hurst.why: Two places can be equally steep and still drive and land very differently.

coherence.label: Grain direction
coherence.what: Whether the slopes face one main direction (1, like rows of ridges or dunes) or every direction (0).
coherence.see_it: Look for lines of ridges running the same way.
coherence.why: Shown as context only: on flat ground the measurement noise is as large as the signal, so it is not used to rank twins.

ridge_pct.label: Ridges
ridge_pct.what: Share of the ground standing more than about 9 m above the ground around it (within 500 m).
ridge_pct.why: Shown as context only: it moves together with steepness, so counting it again would double-count.

valley_pct.label: Hollows
valley_pct.what: Share of the ground lying more than about 9 m below the ground around it (within 500 m).
valley_pct.why: Shown as context only: it moves together with steepness, so counting it again would double-count.

layers.doc: Bits of terrain/<id>/layers_<body>.bin (STANDARDS 10.5): computed on the same 100 m grid as the measures and the mission percentages, so what is drawn is exactly what was counted.

bit0.label: Too steep to land
bit0.what: Ground steeper than the landing slope limit of the site's world (limit and source in the card).

bit1.label: Too steep to drive
bit1.what: Ground steeper than the rover driving slope limit (limit and source in the card).

bit2.label: Ridges
bit2.what: Ground more than about 9 m above its surroundings (500 m radius).

bit3.label: Hollows
bit3.what: Ground more than about 9 m below its surroundings (500 m radius).

mission_pct.what: Share of the ground under the landing (or driving) slope limit, measured every 100 m. The limit comes from a published mission document (linked). It compares ground with a published number; it is not a mission simulation.

scope.detail: Full relief, layers and cross-sections exist for the 16 named sites and their 10 Earth candidates each. The 1,838 Mars places across the planet have measures and Earth twins, but no relief view.
scope.earth_search: The Earth search covers rock ground only: NASADEM from 56 S to 60 N, and Copernicus GLO-30 from 60 N to 84 N. Windows with 20% or more ice are left out.
